# Low-risk allowlist. A PR is low risk only when EVERY changed file matches a pattern
# here and none matches .github/risk-tiers.txt (which always wins).
#
# Anything on neither list is high risk. That's deliberate: the rest of app/ (catalogue,
# models, controllers), factories, a new folder or a new script nobody thought to list
# gets reviewed instead of slipping through. Add to this list on purpose, in its own PR,
# which will itself be high risk.
#
# Read at the PR's BASE commit. fnmatch patterns: `*` also crosses `/`, so folders are
# listed by folder (resources/views/*), never by extension (*.php).

# --- Docs -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Plans, specs, runbooks and design screens. Shell scripts and agent files in here are
# still high (see risk-tiers.txt).
docs/*
*.md
LICENSE

# --- Views and front end ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Blade templates, CSS and browser JS. The service worker is still high.
resources/views/*
resources/css/*
resources/js/*

# --- Static files -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Images can't run; SVG can, and is on the high-risk list.
public/favicon.ico
public/robots.txt
*.png
*.jpg
*.gif
*.webp

# --- Tests ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# tests/TestCase.php and tests/Concerns/* are on the high-risk list: they decide which
# database the tests touch.
tests/*

# --- Dependencies -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Version bumps are low. risk_tier.py separately flags any NEW package in a lockfile and
# any manifest change beyond version numbers (scripts, overrides, new deps, git sources).
composer.json
composer.lock
package.json
package-lock.json
